mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: lower FEDFUNDS levels predict positive 20-day returns. This relationship is continuously active and does not require a threshold condition.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical inverse correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an easing monetary policy, compressing discount rates and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active only when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical rate cuts during 2008-2009 led to market rallies
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% are not significantly positive (mean return < 0.01% or p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in private employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signal a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active only when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% and UNRATE decline exceeds 0.3% over the past 3 months.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.3% in 3 months
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between labor market strength and equity returns
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.3% in 3 months) are not significantly positive (mean return < 0.01% or p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle, defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 2.0% over the past 3 months, signals reduced liquidity and higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical market sell-offs during rate hikes (e.g., 1994, 1999)
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 2.0% are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.01% or p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1500.0 thousand units signals weak economic demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active only when HOUST falls below 1500.0.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between housing starts and equity market performance
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when HOUST is below 1500.0 are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.01% or p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (2017=100) signals a recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active only when INDPRO falls below 100.0.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when INDPRO is below 100.0 are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.01% or p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The signal is always active (no threshold condition) and uses the current level of FEDFUNDS.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% are not significantly positive (mean return < 0.01% or p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (as measured by GDPC1) signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is always active (no threshold condition) because the growth rate is continuously monitored.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between GDP growth and equity market performance
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when GDP growth (GDPC1) is above 2.0% are not significantly positive (mean return < 0.01% or p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
